title: Best practices guide: gateway enforcement is a checkpoint, enforcement belongs at the in-loop hook (Section 3.1)

inline_text:
Origin: PR #9 review thread https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/9#discussion_r4015621290. Fernando flagged this for WG discussion; opening the issue so the call has a written proposal.

**Current text** ([L63](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/e757d350133fea0858dda1deec13dbca923b3cf8/deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md?plain=1#L63)): "Gateway enforcement for any deployment with more than one MCP server: route all agent-to-tool traffic through a single checkpoint ... that enforces OAuth, applies per-tool permission policy, and captures full request/response payloads."

**Proposal.** Keep the gateway as a network checkpoint for remote MCP servers and as the payload capture Section 6 relies on. Move enforcement to a hook inside the agent loop, where every tool call passes regardless of transport. The gateway feeds the hook, it does not replace it.

**Why.**
- A gateway only sees remote MCP traffic. It misses stdio servers ([L47](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/e757d350133fea0858dda1deec13dbca923b3cf8/deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md?plain=1#L47) calls them the most common mode), shell commands, SDK calls and framework connectors.
- It sees each call without the prompt that caused it, so no context-aware policy.
- It routes credentials through itself, it is a single point of failure, and agents on developer machines or in CI walk around it.
- Section 4 already says the execution-layer controls are what bound the damage ([L133](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/e757d350133fea0858dda1deec13dbca923b3cf8/deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md?plain=1#L133)). Section 3.1 should point at the same layer.

Two small neutrality fixes while editing: describe the capability in the body and keep the Cloudflare MCP Portals mention in Section 7; agentgateway is an AAIF project since June 2026 and can be named as one.

Disclosure: the longer version of this argument is my employer's post, https://www.capsulesecurity.io/blog-post/why-mcp-gateways-are-a-bad-idea-and-what-to-do-instead. The hook pattern is specified vendor-neutrally in the OWASP Agent Control Standard, which I contribute to.

Note: I am opening these follow-ups from my personal account. The original review comments on PR #9 are under @bar-capsule, same person.
